hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides change from basic on the left to acidic on the right, and how that affects their reaction with water and with acid.
Notice that X has an oxide that does not react with water but does form a salt with HCl, while its chloride hydrolyses. Which metal fits that amphoteric, insoluble pattern?
Check Y next: its oxide makes a hydroxide and its chloride just dissolves, with no hydrolysis. That points to a strongly basic Group 1 or 2 metal, then see which pairing works together.
walkthrough:
**Sort out what each test tells you**

Think like this. Basic oxides react with acid to make a salt, acidic oxides make acids with water. Chlorides that hydrolyse belong to high charge or non-metal elements like $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{SiCl}_4$, $\text{PCl}_5$.

Simple ionic chlorides like $\text{NaCl}$ just dissolve:
$$\text{NaCl(s)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+(aq) + \text{Cl}^-(aq)$$

**Identify X**

X oxide + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives no reaction, so it is insoluble and not strongly acidic or basic. X oxide + $\text{HCl}$ gives a chloride salt, so it is basic or amphoteric. X chloride + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ hydrolyses.

That matches aluminium perfectly:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl}$$

**Identify Y and Z**

Y oxide + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ forms a hydroxide, Y chloride just dissolves, Y oxide + $\text{HCl}$ forms a salt. That is a basic metal oxide from the left of Period 3, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ or $\text{MgO}$.

Z oxide + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ forms an acid and Z chloride hydrolyses. That is a non-metal on the right of Period 3, such as Si, P or S.

**Test the pairings**

X = Al fits X perfectly. Y = Mg fits Y: $\text{MgO}$ is sparingly soluble but gives $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, $\text{MgCl}_2$ dissolves without strong hydrolysis, and $\text{MgO}$ gives $\text{MgCl}_2$ with HCl. So X is Al and Y is Mg is fully consistent.

options.A: X is Al: Al2O3 is insoluble in water (no reaction), amphoteric so reacts with HCl to give AlCl3 salt, and AlCl3 hydrolyses in water. Y is Mg: MgO reacts to give Mg(OH)2 hydroxide, MgCl2 dissolves simply, and MgO gives MgCl2 salt with HCl. Both fit the table.
options.B: X cannot be Si. SiO2 is acidic and does not form a chloride salt with HCl, it shows no reaction with HCl. SiCl4 also hydrolyses, but the oxide with acid test fails for Si.
options.C: Y cannot be Al. Al2O3 shows no reaction with water, it does not form a hydroxide solution. AlCl3 also hydrolyses rather than just dissolving. Z could be P, but the Y part makes the whole statement wrong.
options.D: Y could be Na, since Na2O forms NaOH and NaCl just dissolves. But Z cannot be Al, because Al2O3 does not form an acid with water and Al2O3 with HCl forms a salt, not hydrolysis. The Z description needs a non-metal oxide.
